To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the amplitude of N1 is higher in the condition of counting than listening and the latency is not different in the conditions of counting and listening.
the amplitude and latency of the N1, N1 and P300 ERP components do not depend on age of subjects.

the amplitude of the N1 component of the ERP was significantly greater in the counting task compared to the listening task, and that the latency of the P300 component was significantly greater in young examinees than in mature examinees in the counting task.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of age on the amplitude-time parameters of components N1 N2 and P3 of the auditory event-related potentials (ERPs).
the study of age-related changes in amplitude-time parameters of components N1,N2 and P300, and also with the analysis of the influence of complexity of the task on these parameters.
the study of the age changes in the auditory evoked potential in the context of the cognitive processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the amplitude-time parameters of components N1 and N2 are age-dependent.
the age-related differences in ERP parameters are likely to reflect changes in neural processes that underlie the generation of ERP components.
the age-related changes in ERP components are not uniform, but rather depend on the specific component, the age group, and the task.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the amplitude and latency of components N1 and N2 of acoustic evoked potentials are age-dependent.
the age of the person is not a factor of the complexity of the task, and the age of the examinee is a factor of the task.
ERP is an effective tool to study the age-related changes in the brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amplitude-time parametres components N1, and N2 and P3 do not differ in the situation of account and listening of the sounds in both age group.
the age-related changes of amplitude and latency of components N1 and N2 are not revealed.
the age differences in ERP parameters are task dependent.
